 Africa Cup of Nations Qualification
 LIVE: Gambia vs Ivory Coast | 2027 AFCON Qualifiers
 Gambia hosts Ivory Coast in the 2027 AFCON Qualifiers after a 2-1 defeat in their previous meeting. The Elephants aim to clinch qualification, while the Scorpions seek revenge on home soil.
 Watch Gambia vs Ivory Coast LIVE on beIN SPORTS 
 Gambia vs Ivory Coast: How and Where to Watch LIVE
 Matchday 4 of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers brings another important showdown on Tuesday, November 17, as Gambia welcomes Ivory Coast to Independence Stadium in Bakau .
 The Elephants lead Group C with nine points after winning all three of their matches, while Gambia sits second with six points. Kickoff is scheduled for 11:00 AM ET / 8:00 AM PT , with English-language coverage beginning at 10:50 AM ET / 7:50 AM PT on beIN SPORTS CONNECT. 
 Gambia Looks for Revenge With Musa Barrow Leading the Attack
 Gambia , managed by Johnathan McKinstry , made an impressive start to its qualification campaign with two victories that established the Scorpions as serious contenders in Group C.
 The team opened with a 2-1 win over Somalia , thanks to goals from Ebrima Colley and Muhammed Badamosi , before producing a remarkable comeback against Ghana .
 After falling two goals behind, Gambia recovered to claim a memorable 4-2 away victory, demonstrating its attacking potential and resilience.
 However, that winning streak came to an end on Thursday, November 12, when the Scorpions suffered a 2-1 defeat against Ivory Coast at the Stade de la Paix in Bouaké .
 The visitors found themselves two goals down within the opening 24 minutes, but Musa Barrow reduced the deficit in the 38th minute and kept his team's hopes alive.
 Barrow's return has been particularly important for McKinstry , who also welcomed back Yankuba Minteh of Brighton after both players missed the opening qualifying fixtures through injury.
 With seven goals scored and five conceded across three matches, Gambia has shown plenty of attacking ability but will need greater defensive consistency to challenge the group leaders.
 Ivory Coast Targets Early Qualification After Another Victory
 Ivory Coast enters Tuesday's encounter in excellent form, having won all three of its matches in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers under head coach Hervé Renard .
 The Elephants began their campaign with consecutive 2-0 victories over Ghana and Somalia before extending their perfect record with a 2-1 home win against Gambia .
 During that latest meeting, Malick Yalcouyé opened the scoring in the 17th minute following an assist from Nicolas Pépé .
 Just seven minutes later, Elye Wahi doubled the advantage after taking advantage of a defensive mistake, scoring his first international goal for Ivory Coast .
 Although Musa Barrow pulled one back before halftime, Renard's side managed to protect its lead and move three points clear at the top of Group C.
 With six goals scored and only one conceded, the Elephants have combined attacking efficiency with defensive solidity throughout the campaign.
 The squad also features experienced players such as Franck Kessié , Ibrahim Sangaré , and Amad Diallo , giving Renard several options as he looks to maintain his team's momentum.
 The French coach, who guided Ivory Coast to the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations title, now has an opportunity to secure qualification with two matches remaining.
 Can Gambia End Ivory Coast's Perfect Run?
 The return fixture between Gambia and Ivory Coast could play a decisive role in determining the final Group C standings.
 After three rounds, the Elephants lead with nine points, followed by Gambia with six, Ghana with three, and Somalia without a point.
 The top two teams will qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations , which will be hosted by Kenya , Tanzania , and Uganda .
 A fourth consecutive victory would take Ivory Coast to 12 points and guarantee its place at the continental tournament. For Gambia , securing a positive result is essential to protecting its position in the qualification race, particularly with Ghana also challenging for the second available spot.
 The first meeting highlighted the difference between the two teams, with the Elephants recording 19 shots compared to just six from the Scorpions .
 Nevertheless, playing at Independence Stadium offers Gambia a valuable opportunity to respond, especially with attacking talents such as Musa Barrow and Yankuba Minteh available.
 The hosts will be determined to avoid another difficult start and deliver a stronger performance against one of the continent's most established national teams.
